comparison: Perfect agreement on DDI2-independence claims (C4, C25, C28, C29, C30, C31, C32, C78, C79). Both OpenEval and all three peer reviewers find this conclusion strongly supported by convergent experimental evidence across multiple cell lines and genetic approaches.

Perfect agreement on transcription-independence claims (C5, C26, C33, C34, C35). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers find the temporal data convincingly demonstrates that activity recovery precedes mRNA upregulation, establishing transcription-independent early recovery.

Disagreement on protein synthesis requirement claims (C6, C36, C37). OpenEval finds CHX blocking experiments provide strong support, rating as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, expressing concerns that the mechanistic interpretation needs stronger orthogonal evidence beyond the CHX data alone.

Disagreement on translational upregulation claims (C38, C39, C40, C41, C80). OpenEval finds polysome profiling data sufficient for SUPPORTED rating. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, specifically critiquing reliance on two replicates and requesting additional data on protein levels and assembled proteasome complexes over time.

Agreement on main conclusion claims (C7, C27, C42, C43, C60). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers support the existence of a novel DDI2-independent, transcription-independent pathway, though both acknowledge the molecular mechanism remains uncharacterized and uncertain.

Significant disagreement on mechanistic model claims (C65, C66, C68, C69). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, acknowledging speculation but noting consistency with data. Peer reviewers rate as UNSUPPORTED, explicitly stating the assembly-based mechanism lacks experimental support and remains speculative, with alternative mechanisms being equally plausible.

Agreement on clinical significance claims (C1, C18). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN/speculative. OpenEval notes lack of clinical data or resistance studies. Peer reviewer questions clinical applicability due to single-pulse vs. multiple-treatment protocol differences.

OpenEval finds claims C44 and C45 (contextualizing findings within prior literature on DDI2/Nrf1 partial contribution) are SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific literature contextualization claims.

OpenEval finds claims C46-C50 (addressing discrepancies with prior studies and cell-type differences) are SUPPORTED with appropriate acknowledgment and citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific discrepancy resolution claims.

OpenEval rates claims C55, C56, C57, C59 (speculative hypotheses about DDI2's role in PI sensitivity beyond recovery pathway) as UNCERTAIN, noting they are appropriately presented as possibilities but lack direct experimental testing. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval finds claims C2, C3, C20, C21, C22, C23, C30 (established background on DDI2/Nrf1 pathway) are SUPPORTED by appropriate citations and authors' own data. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background knowledge claims, though C30 overlaps with R1 context.

OpenEval finds claims C8-C17 (background on proteasome inhibitors, clinical use, and pharmacokinetics) are SUPPORTED with appropriate citations providing clinical context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.

OpenEval finds claims C63, C64, C67 (prior literature on nascent subunit degradation supporting the proposed model) are SUPPORTED by appropriate citations and Figure 4a data. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though this literature basis is implicitly questioned in peer R6's critique of the mechanistic model.
